announcements.title: Eleven baptisms by the river
announcements.body: They came at night, and the water was cold, and nobody minded. Eleven believers, three of them from one household, walked into the river with their pastor while two brothers kept watch on the road. Each one went under the water carrying an old life and came up without it. There was no singing, because singing carries. Instead the pastor spoke each name softly, and the church mouthed the amen. By morning the authorities had heard something and came to the bank, and found wet grass, and footprints going in every direction, and nothing else. The fellowship asks you not to pray for ease. They ask you to pray for the eleven, that the first year of their faith would put down roots no interrogation can pull up. God went before us. He is still there ahead of you too.

announcements.title: A word for today
announcements.body: I just learned a few things today.

announcements.title: August prayer calendar is coming
announcements.body: One nation each day through August, paired with a short intercession you can pray with your fellowship. The calendar names thirty one nations where the church walks carefully, and for each one, a single specific request gathered from leaders who live there. Not headlines; requests. The kind a brother writes when you ask him what he actually needs prayed over. Print it, fold it into your Bible, and take the month slowly. When the calendar posts here, it will also carry a short note on how the July calendar was answered, because the network should see what the Lord did with its praying.

announcements.title: Prayer for the gathering in Jos
announcements.body: Leaders from three states meet quietly this weekend to pray over the harvest season. Some are driving through the night to be there, on roads that are not kind after dark. Set aside a moment for them today: for safe travel there and home again, for wisdom in what they plan together, for the ones who could not risk the journey and will be present only in the prayers of the others, and for joy, because these gatherings are rare and the brothers have missed one another. They have asked for no details to be shared beyond this. It is enough for the network to know they are gathered, and to stand with them from wherever you are.

announcements.title: You who plant in hard soil
announcements.body: The seed you cannot see is still the seed God is keeping. Do not measure the harvest by the corner of the field you can watch. There is a sower who went out before you, and there will be reapers after you, and the field was never yours to carry alone. Some of you have preached for a year into what feels like stone. Some of you have buried more than you have baptised this season. Hear this from an old man who has watched sixty harvests: the stone is not the whole story. Under it, where no one applauds and nothing seems to move, the root is finding water. Stay at your post. Water what you were given. The Lord of the harvest has not forgotten the corner of the field where you stand, and what He keeps, no drought and no decree can take.

announcements.title: Verify before you add: a security reminder
announcements.body: Before adding an unknown contact to any fellowship group, confirm them through someone you already trust. Two minutes of checking protects everyone in the room. This is not suspicion; it is shepherding. A wolf does not announce itself, and in three regions this quarter we have seen friendly strangers ask for group invitations within days of meeting a leader. Here is the practice we ask of every leader on the network: first, never forward a group link to someone you have not met through a trusted brother or sister. Second, when someone new asks to join, name one person who can vouch for them, and actually ask that person. Third, if no one can vouch, meet them yourself first, in person or by call, before they enter any room where others are visible. The two minutes this takes has already protected fellowships this year in ways we will not describe here. Guard the door, and the room stays warm.

announcements.title: Field briefing: the state of the persecuted church
announcements.body: A short external briefing with regional summaries and specific ways to pray. Opens outside the app.

announcements.title: Where the church stands: a mid-year reading
announcements.body: A longer look at what the network has carried this year. In the first half of this year the network grew by more fellowships than in all of last year, and not evenly: the strongest growth came from the hardest places, which should not surprise anyone who has read the book of Acts. We watched one fellowship scatter under pressure in February and regather by May as four smaller ones, each with its own leader, each quieter and harder to find than the original. That pattern, scattering that becomes multiplication, has repeated on three continents. We also carried losses. Two leaders were detained this spring. Both are home. Both asked, before anything else, whether their people had kept meeting. They had. Read the full briefing for the regional summaries, what the pattern of it teaches about endurance, and the specific ways the network is asked to pray through August. Read slowly. This one is not news; it is testimony in aggregate.

announcements.title: Written together: a word from three fellowships
announcements.body: Three fellowships in three time zones wrote this in one shared evening of prayer, passing a single document between them as each finished its watch. What they asked for, each for the others, is worth reading twice. The fellowship in the east prayed for the one in the west to be bold, because boldness is what they themselves lack. The one in the west prayed for the east to be hidden well, because hiddenness is what they have never needed. And the third, which meets in a country between the two, prayed that both would remember that the church is one body under one Lord, and that no border on any map has ever interrupted the Spirit. We publish it as they wrote it, unedited, because the network should hear how its own members pray for one another when they think no one else is listening.
